applicability: Predicting whether the canonical material pair can statically hold a support on a measured slope
Cross-checking the L1.1 flat-floor breakaway bracket by an independent geometry
claim: For the exact L1.2 free block on seven independent real-Jolt slopes with the authored friction 0.6 material pair at 60 Hz, post-step hold-versus-slide classification brackets the static threshold between the 30 degree and 32 degree slopes. This is consistent with tan(30 deg) = 0.577 below and tan(32 deg) = 0.625 above the authored coefficient, and gravity normal/tangent decomposition balanced on every measured slope.

evidence.certification_claim_boundary: This campaign can certify only the L1.0-L1.7 contact-engine observations named by the exact source-pinned programs. L1.8 and the knowledge guard are supplementary constraints. It establishes no articulated load-bearing limb, standing, bracing, fall arrest, getting up, walking, accepted knowledge, automatic creature guidance, or per-foot allocation of reconstructed whole-system load.

programs.claim_scope: The declared incline fixture brackets static retention and downhill sliding.

failure_boundaries: Does not cover other friction values, materials, curvature, or surface roughness
Does not cover intermediate unmeasured angles inside 30-32 degrees beyond the bracket itself
Does not cover articulated bodies or actuated limbs on slopes
Does not establish standing, bracing, fall arrest, getting up, or walking
mechanism: On a slope of angle theta a static body's required friction ratio is tan(theta). The measured hold at 30 degrees and slide at 32 degrees brackets the effective static coefficient for this material pair inside 0.577-0.625, which contains the authored 0.6. Classification uses post-step motion, not the pre-constraint callback candidate documented by L1.1.
